annotations.text:
What breaks, and where

The map is sized from the hero's HEIGHT (height: 82% + aspect-ratio 1/1),
so a tall window grows it sideways into the copy column. That is the
"sometimes" — it tracks window height, not width.

Two separate faults:
1. Tall/short desktop — blocks sit under the headline, subhead and input.
2. Narrow screens — the sun clips the bottom-right of the address field.

Measured across 17 window sizes: 10 fail WCAG AA (4.5:1) for the grey
subhead against what is actually painted behind it.

Option A — the map gets its own column

left is pinned past the copy's right edge, so overlap is impossible by
construction, at any window size.

Holds at 17 of 17 sizes.

Trade: loses the bleed. The map no longer runs under the input, which was
the point of the original composition. On a short wide window the map gets
noticeably smaller than it is today.

Option B — the scrim knows where the copy ends

The map is untouched. The white scrim is redefined to stay opaque out to
the copy column's real right edge, then fade over 220px:

  --copy-edge: calc(max((100% - 1360px)/2, 0px) + 40px + 680px)

Holds at 17 of 17 sizes.

Trade: the map is still full-size behind the copy, just covered. On very
tall windows a lot of it is hidden — you are paying for blocks nobody sees.

This is my recommendation for DESKTOP: it fixes the fault without giving
up the composition you picked.

Option C — fade the map out under the copy

A mask on the map itself, so blocks dissolve rather than being covered:
  mask-image: linear-gradient(90deg, transparent 4%, #000 42%)

Holds at only 12 of 17 sizes — it FAILS.

A mask thins the blocks, it does not remove them. Partly-faded red under
grey text still lands between 1.8:1 and 4.4:1, under the 4.5 floor. Shown
here because it is the prettiest idea of the three and it is worth seeing
why it does not survive measurement.

Phone & tablet — three ways out

Left column is what ships now plus the sun fix: the map drops below the
copy at 58vw. It reads, but it is a heavy slab hanging under the form.

N1 WASH — the whole city sits fully behind the copy, contained and pale.
  Trade: to clear 4.5:1 the wash has to drop to 9% opacity. Any stronger
  and the grey subhead fails. At 9% it is barely there — closer to paper
  texture than a map. Honest version of "put it fully behind".

N2 MOTIF — the city shrinks to a mark above the copy, clamp(120px, 26vw,
  240px), with the sun scaled to match. Whole shape visible, nothing
  overlaps, and the hero gets ~90px shorter so the address field is
  reachable without scrolling.
  Trade: small. You lose the "every block in New York" scale.

N3 BAND — the city crops to a horizon strip along the bottom,
  clamp(150px, 30vw, 260px) tall, with the sun rising off it.
  Trade: cropped, so it reads as texture rather than a recognisable NYC.

All three clear 4.5:1 at 7 narrow sizes from 360 to 1024. They are
independent of the desktop choice — any of them pairs with A or B.

Both faults, both fixed

The narrow-screen sun clash is orthogonal to the desktop one and is
fixed the same way in every option: give the map 62px of headroom
below the copy instead of 14px, so the sun — which rides ~38px above
the map's top edge — clears the address field.

  padding-bottom: calc(min(58vw, 520px) + 62px)
